subject: POC resource plan & success criteria — Datawave
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Amy Park <amy.park@datawave.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: POC resource plan & success criteria — Datawave

Hi Amy / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo today — good conversation. Below is a concise recap and a proposed short POC plan so we can lock resources and timelines. I tried to keep the ask minimal while giving you a realistic environment to exercise inference economics and latency under expected traffic.

Recap (what you told us)
- Primary workloads: chat completions and short-form generation (avg prompt 120 tokens, avg response 200 tokens)
- Peak concurrency expected during test: ~60 concurrent users; target steady-state QPS ~50, short bursts to ~200 for replay testing
- Dataset: ~15k prompts for eval; data includes PII-obfuscated examples (we'll need encryption-in-transit & at-rest assurances)

Proposed POC (3-week window, non-production)
1) Environment
   - Reserved: 2 x A100 80GB (reserved for 24/7 during POC)
   - Autoscaling: allow burst to 4 x A100 for short windows (policy: scale up when CPU/GPU utilization >70% for 60s, scale down after 5m of <40%)
   - Networking: VPC peering + TLS; option for customer-managed KMS if required
2) Success criteria (pass/fail focused)
   - Latency: generation p50 < 250ms, p95 < 950ms for the chat path with 200-token outputs at steady-state load
   - Throughput: sustain 50 QPS for sustained test and handle 200 QPS bursts for at least 3 minutes without tail latency spikes >2x baseline
   - Cost signal: < $0.XX per 1k tokens (we'll provide estimated bucket based on actual run)
   - Quality: automated eval hunts show no >5% drop in core intent accuracy vs your baseline across the 15k eval set
3) Ownership & timeline
   - Redwood: infra provisioning, model variant options, runbook for scaling tests, cost estimate
   - Datawave: provide eval set, baseline metrics, approval for test windows, PII compliance sign-off
   - Target start: week of Oct 25 (flexible by one week)

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf (contains detailed steps and suggested prompts), capacity-estimate-quote.xlsx (preliminary cost/VM mix)

Next steps (action items)
- Amy: confirm start week (Oct 25 vs Oct 18) and whether you require customer-managed KMS or SOC2 evidence up front
- Ben: share the 15k eval set link or a sample subset (S3 link)
- Redwood (Rafael/Grace): provision temporary reserved pool and publish estimate once Amy confirms start date

If this looks good I can convert to a mutual action plan and send a short MPA doc.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0148

Date: 2027-10-03T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC resource plan & success criteria — Datawave

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Token assumptions: your numbers look right for the chat path. Can you confirm end-to-end tokenization (prompt+resp) will be accounted for in the cost estimate?
2) Eval set: we'll share an S3 link with a 1k sample by EOD tomorrow; full 15k by next Friday
3) Security: we definitely need SOC2 Type II evidence and prefer customer-managed KMS if feasible — is that supported in the POC?
4) Start date: Oct 25 works better for our infra team (Oct 18 is tight)
5) Pricing: can you provide a short delta between reserved-only vs reserved+autoscale? we want to understand projected overage costs if bursts materialize

If you can address those points, we can sign off internally and commit to the Oct 25 start.

Thanks,
Amy
Amy Park
Director, Platform Engineering — Datawave Inc
amy.park@datawave.com | +1 (617) 555-2199
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Amy Park <amy.park@datawave.com>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@datawave.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC resource plan & success criteria — Datawave

Amy — great, appreciate the quick turnaround. Short answers inline and an updated action list below.

1) Token accounting: yes — our cost model will include both prompt + response tokens; I'll attach a short worked example in the estimate.
2) Eval set: perfect — we'll start with the 1k sample for early functional checks and then run full eval when we have 15k.
3) Security/KMS: customer-managed KMS is supported in the Private deployment; for hosted POC we can enable envelope encryption with your KMS via an integration or provide SOC2 Type II attestation and audit logs. We'll flag this as a gating item in the MPA.
4) Start date: Oct 25 - locked.
5) Pricing delta: Rafael/Grace will follow up with reserved vs reserved+burst numbers (short spreadsheet). Expect a conservative estimate for burst capacity costs that differentiates reserved baseline and 1-hour burst scenarios.

Updated responsibilities & dates
- By Oct 08: Datawave to share 1k sample + decision on KMS/SOC2 gating
- Oct 18–22: Redwood provision reserved pool (staging) and run smoke tests internally
- Oct 25–Nov 12: Joint POC window (3 weeks) — formal eval on week 3

Next actions (short):
- Amy: share 1k sample + confirm KMS preference by Oct 08
- Ben: confirm preferred test windows for burst simulation (two 10–30 minute windows during week 2)
- Rafael/Grace: send reserved vs reserved+burst cost sheet by Oct 06

I'll prepare a short MPA and send for signatures once Rafael confirms pricing rows. Let me know if you'd like us to run a quick pre-POC load test with a simulated 200 QPS burst to validate autoscaling.

Best,
Lauren
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: POC resource plan & success criteria — Datawave — action: capacity & pricing

Folks — forwarding the thread with Datawave. Key asks for us: locked start week Oct 25, customer likely wants customer-managed KMS or SOC2 evidence, 2 x A100 reserved baseline with autoscale to 4 for bursts. Please produce the following by Oct 06:

1) Capacity runbook: exact instance sizes, expected GPU memory headroom given 200-token outputs, and estimated sustained throughput per node
2) Pricing sheet: reserved baseline vs reserved+1-hr burst scenario (line items for GPU-hours, storage, network) — use conservative utilization assumptions
3) Ops run: recommended autoscale thresholds and cooldowns we will run during the pre-POC smoke test (Oct 18–22)

Would appreciate a brief note if any of this is materially off (e.g., need more GPUs to meet p50/p95 targets). Datawave asked for a worked token-cost example — include that on the pricing sheet.

Thanks — low-lift but time-sensitive.

— Lauren
